_pricing_note: RESOLVED 2026-09-04 via Microsoft support ticket API TrackingID#2608200050000071 — the previous belief here (pricing is unwritable for this account, leave it untouched) was WRONG and caused a real 'InvalidParameterValue: Base is not a valid PriceId' rejection on every submit-ms-store.ps1 PUT from 2026-08-20 onward. Microsoft's own Engineering Team confirmed: GET returns 'Base' as an internal sentinel that can NEVER be written back on PUT; PUT requires a concrete tier instead — for isAdvancedPricingModel=true accounts (WhisPaste's case) that means 'Free' or Tier1001+ (legacy Tier2-Tier96 are rejected for this pricing model). pricing.priceId must be present with a valid value in EVERY PUT (the classic Submission API does a full replacement) — omitting it silently defaults to Free. scripts/submit-ms-store.ps1 now reads default.PriceId from here, validates it, and writes it explicitly on every submission. REQUIRED ONE-TIME SETUP: replace the placeholder above with the Tier10xx value matching WhisPaste's real price — look it up in Partner Center > Pricing and availability > the tier-to-price conversion table (NOT guessable/linear like the old Tier2-Tier96 scale — this is a separate, non-linear numbering per Microsoft). The script refuses to run (hard error) until this is a real Tier10xx/Free value, on purpose — see the script header for why a silent wrong guess is worse than a loud failure. Full trail: ~/.claude/infrastructure/microsoft-partner-center.md §12, docs/store-release.md.
